title: Genomic Medicine and Precision Therapeutics
answer: Polygenic risk, gene editing design, pharmacogenomics, epigenetic age and rare disease diagnosis.

children.name: Polygenic Risk Scores
children.blurb: A polygenic risk score is a single number that sums the small effects of many common genetic variants linked to a disease.

children.name: Gene Editing Guide Design
children.blurb: Gene editing guide design is the computational task of selecting short RNA sequences that direct a CRISPR nuclease to a specific genomic site while minimizing off-target binding and maximizing on-target activity.

children.name: Pharmacogenomics
children.blurb: Pharmacogenomics is the study of how inherited genetic variation changes a person's response to drugs, including metabolism, transport, and target binding.

children.name: Epigenetic Aging Clocks
children.blurb: Epigenetic aging clocks are models that estimate biological age from DNA methylation patterns at specific CpG sites, often differing from chronological age.

children.name: Rare Disease Diagnosis
children.blurb: Rare disease diagnosis uses machine learning to identify conditions that affect small numbers of patients, often from genomic and phenotypic data.

sections.body: This field applies machine learning to DNA and RNA data to predict disease risk, design gene edits, match drugs to genetic profiles, estimate biological age, and find causes of rare conditions. Current work includes models that score many small genetic variants together for common diseases, algorithms that choose target sites for CRISPR tools, systems that flag drug gene interactions, clocks that estimate age from methylation patterns, and classifiers that rank candidate genes in undiagnosed patients. These are not hypothetical, they run on real sequence data and clinical records in research and some hospital settings.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Polygenic risk scores are reproducible in research cohorts but often perform poorly across different ancestries and are not reliable for individual prediction. Gene editing guide design is good at predicting off target cuts in the lab but less certain in living tissue. Pharmacogenomics has solid evidence for a small set of gene drug pairs, yet most drug responses remain unexplained. Epigenetic aging clocks correlate with chronological age and some health outcomes, but what they measure biologically is still debated. Rare disease diagnosis tools can shorten the search for a known gene, but many patients still get no answer. The honest limit is that most models are validated on retrospective data, not prospective clinical use, and the site tracks 1000 medical AI models, which shows scale but not clinical proof.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader wanting to understand risk prediction for common diseases would start with Polygenic Risk Scores, which explains how many small variants are combined and why ancestry matters. Gene Editing Guide Design covers the computational side of choosing CRISPR targets and predicting repair outcomes. Pharmacogenomics connects genetic variants to drug metabolism and response, useful for seeing where testing has clear evidence. Epigenetic Aging Clocks describes methylation based age estimates and their current research status. Rare Disease Diagnosis shows how AI ranks candidate genes and variants for patients without a known cause, and it pairs naturally with the polygenic and pharmacogenomics pages when a diagnosis leads to treatment questions.
